newsitem.title: USA: Xavier says CFO quits, co faces delisting.
newsitem.headline: Xavier says CFO quits, co faces delisting.

text.p: Xavier Corp said Wednesday that its chief financial officer resigned and that a pending debt conversion may result in extreme dilution of its stock.
The company also said Nasdaq has notified it of plans to delist its shares.

Xavier said it did not know the reason for high recent trading volume of its common stock, but it said it a substantial sell-side imbalance in the stock may have been created by short sellers or trading on unsubstantiated rumors.
The company said it recognized the substantial dilution created by issuing the shares, but said it had no other immediate financing alternatives to maintain its Russian contract concessions.
The company said it raised another $6.8 million of interim financing during the past three months through private placement of convertible debentures in overseas markets.
Xavier said those funds supported its operations and allowed it to buy materials and pay contractors to start the "western phase" of operations at the Kamennoye West license area in Western Siberia.

The company said additional financing, if available, would allow the drilling and hook-up to sales lines of the 30 wells which have been drilled and cased by its Russian contractor to the top of the oil-bearing Cretaceous formation.
Xavier said it expects the completion of the wells will begin this summer.
It said it continues to negotitate with several possible sources of additional working capital to fulfill its contract obligations in the development of its Russian oil properties.
Xavier also said it expects to file its 10-K in June.
